title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
subject: Number theory
claim: Every Dirichlet L-function, including the Riemann zeta, has no zeros past 7/8. A big step toward the full Riemann hypothesis.
why: Primes are the locks of the internet. Every bank login and chat encryption leans on how primes are distributed. Tighter control of zeta zeros means tighter guarantees for that math.

title: Full Birch Swinnerton-Dyer formula in low rank
subject: Number theory
claim: Proves the full BSD formula for elliptic curves of Selmer corank zero and one.
why: Elliptic curves guard Bitcoin wallets and secure messaging. BSD connects their algebra to their analytics, so progress here hardens the foundations under modern cryptography.

title: Hilbert's tenth problem over Q
subject: Logic
claim: No algorithm can decide whether an integer-coefficient polynomial has a rational solution.
why: It draws a hard border around what computers can ever do. Solver and AI verification tools must respect this wall when reasoning about equations.

title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
subject: Number theory
claim: Pi cannot be approximated by fractions any better than the theoretical optimum, exponent exactly 2.
why: Sets the gold standard for approximating constants in scientific computing. Numerical libraries now know the best error bound they can hope for with pi.

title: Rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
subject: Geometry
claim: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and products of K3 surfaces.
why: The Hodge conjecture is a million-dollar Millennium problem about shapes defined by equations. Cracking big cases guides string theory geometry and next generation encryption shapes.

title: Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension
subject: Analysis
claim: Resolves how large a point set must be before its distance set fills an interval.
why: Radar, medical imaging, and sensor networks all reconstruct scenes from distance data. This tells engineers the minimum sensor density that guarantees full coverage.

title: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
subject: Analysis
claim: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in 3D and 4D: needle sets must be fat.
why: Kakeya sets model how waves and signals can focus into tiny regions. Results feed antenna design, optics, and understanding rogue wave formation.

title: Symmetric and general Mahler conjectures
subject: Convex geometry
claim: Resolves both Mahler conjectures plus symplectic width: the cube minimizes volume product.
why: Volume products sit at the heart of optimization and packing problems, from warehouse logistics to error correcting codes. A century old gap is now closed.

title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
subject: Geometry
claim: The triangular lattice minimizes energy for a wide class of potentials: mathematically the best arrangement.
why: Nature packs honeycombs and atoms this way. Proof confirms optimal layouts for materials science, 5G sphere packings, and error correcting signal constellations.

title: Unique Games and optimal approximation thresholds
subject: Computer science
claim: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture and pins down optimal approximation thresholds.
why: Delivery routing, chip design, and scheduling rely on approximation algorithms. This result maps exactly how good those algorithms can ever get.

title: Derandomization: L = RL = BPL
subject: Computer science
claim: Randomness adds no power to logarithmic space computation.
why: Randomized algorithms run our networks and databases. Removing their need for randomness means cheaper, reproducible, and more secure low memory computation.

title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4
subject: Computer science
claim: Proves matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over C.
why: Matrix multiplication powers AI training, graphics, and science simulations. A smaller exponent is a direct speedup for every GPU workload on Earth.

title: Integer multiplication below n log n
subject: Computer science
claim: Multiplies n-bit integers faster than n log n at every input length.
why: Big number arithmetic underlies encryption and banking. Faster multiplication trims latency and energy for every secure transaction.

title: Almost-linear-time exact matching
subject: Computer science
claim: Finds exact matchings in general graphs in almost linear time.
why: Matching pairs workers to jobs, donors to patients, riders to drivers. Near linear time means planetary scale assignment problems become routine.

title: Erdos reciprocal-sum and Szemeredi bounds
subject: Combinatorics
claim: Proves Erdos's reciprocal-sum conjecture with quasipolynomial Szemeredi bounds.
why: Guarantees hidden patterns inside large datasets, from prime numbers to sensor logs. Pattern mining tools inherit stronger mathematical guarantees.

title: Mezard-Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
subject: Probability
claim: Proves the hierarchical cavity formula for diluted spin glasses.
why: Spin glass math secretly governs neural networks and combinatorial optimization. This unlocks better understanding of why deep learning training works.

title: Exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
subject: Quantum
claim: Proves N(6) = 3, resolving Zauner's conjecture on measurement bases.
why: Mutually unbiased bases are the alphabet of quantum cryptography. Knowing the exact limit in dimension six fixes what quantum key distribution can achieve there.

title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set
subject: Quantum
claim: Polynomial-time uniform quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set.
why: Factoring breaks RSA encryption. Making it work over realistic fixed hardware brings the post quantum migration deadline closer and more concrete.

title: Bloch's law and spontaneous ferromagnetic order
subject: Physics
claim: Proves Bloch's T3/2 law with exact coefficients plus spontaneous magnetization.
why: Magnets store our data, from hard drives to MRI machines. Exact low temperature laws let engineers design denser and more stable magnetic memory.

title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov Maxwell
subject: PDE
claim: Large-data global existence and smoothness for the 3D relativistic Vlasov Maxwell system.
why: These equations describe hot plasma in fusion reactors and space. Global smoothness means simulations of clean fusion energy rest on solid ground.
